ABOUT NISCHHAL RAJ SUBBA
I DESIGN BY STAYING CLOSE TO THE PRODUCT AND CLOSE TO THE BUILD.
I DESIGN BY STAYING CLOSE TO THE PRODUCT AND CLOSE TO THE BUILD.

I’m a Nepal-based product designer working remotely. My work spans UX architecture, interface design, design systems, technical websites and implementation handoff.

I started in agency and client work, which taught me to move between industries and explain design decisions to people with very different priorities. Product roles pushed the work deeper: more states, longer-lived systems, permissions, data, engineering constraints and the consequences of decisions that cannot be solved by a nicer component.

That is the part of design I enjoy most. I like products where the brief is incomplete and the interface has to make a complicated system easier to reason about. I care about hierarchy, state language, recovery, responsive behavior and the quiet rules that make a product feel predictable.

I also stay close to implementation. I do not need to own the front end on every project, but understanding browser behavior, component constraints and UI QA makes my design work more practical and my handoff less theatrical.

02 · STATE
Design what happens when the happy path stops.

Waiting, errors, permissions, empty states and recovery are product behavior, not cleanup copy.

03 · BUILD

Responsive rules, component behavior and QA should survive without a designer narrating every frame.

UX AUDIT + REMEDIATION
FIND THE FRICTION BEFORE PAYING TO REDESIGN EVERYTHING.
FIND THE FRICTION BEFORE PAYING TO REDESIGN EVERYTHING.

A useful UX audit separates visible symptoms from the product decisions causing them. I review flows, hierarchy, content, interaction states, responsive behavior, accessibility and implementation quality, then turn findings into a prioritized fix plan.

WHEN THIS IS USEFUL
USEFUL WHEN A PRODUCT FEELS INCONSISTENT OR DIFFICULT BUT THE TEAM NEEDS EVIDENCE AND PRIORITIES BEFORE COMMITTING TO A LARGER REDESIGN.
TYPICAL SCOPE
Severity-ranked findings with evidence
Flow and information-architecture review
Accessibility and responsive checks
State, feedback and recovery review
Practical remediation guidance and priorities
HOW I APPROACH IT
MAKE THE PRODUCT DECISION EXPLICIT BEFORE MAKING THE SCREEN LOOK FINISHED.
01 · CONTEXT
Understand the job and the constraint.

Users, evidence, business goal, technical limits and the current behavior that is creating friction.

02 · STRUCTURE
Resolve flow, hierarchy and states.

Turn the problem into reviewable decisions before high-fidelity design makes ambiguity expensive.

03 · DELIVERY
Design for the implementation.

Responsive rules, components, interaction notes and QA make the work useful after handoff.

Neverwinter Live Parser

A live parser that turns noisy combat events into readable performance information while keeping uncertainty and incomplete data visible instead of pretending every number is equally trustworthy.

HOW FINDINGS BECOME A FIX PLAN

Each finding should identify the route and task, reproduction steps, expected and observed behavior, supporting evidence and a test for the fix.

Priority follows the consequence: a blocked core task or unsafe action needs attention before a recoverable delay; a cosmetic inconsistency comes later. Frequency, affected users and available workarounds can change that order.

For example, a failed submission that discards the message is more urgent than inconsistent spacing. The report should make that distinction explicit so the team can choose what to fix first.
